verdict.rationale: GitHub's first-party docs describe the full SSH flow: check for existing keys, generate a new SSH key, add it to the ssh-agent, and add the public key to your GitHub.com account so Git operations authenticate over SSH. They also confirm that SSH can be used to read and write repository data. The community items are about outages and other features, not SSH, so they were ignored. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the SSH setup works as described, and evidence for details such as testing the connection or supported key types.
